cases.title: Findings: Inaccurate injury listing
cases.text:
The league has finished its investigation of the Terrors injury report (opened in week 8, 2045). Investigators concluded the Terrors knew before they filed the report that Aisake Stonesky (RB) was injured and had missed every practice that week, and listed him with no injury designation anyway. Practice attendance sheets and the athletic training staff's notes both show the injury was documented before the filing.

Original matter: The Terrors left a player off the injury report who had missed practice all week. The player is one of the club's best known. The timing drew interest from the league's integrity unit. Yuna Feldmeier told reporters the report was 'a formality'.

WHERE THINGS STAND. In week 8 you fined the club $500K and asked for this investigation. That fine stands. Anything you choose below is imposed in addition to it. The club has no earlier injury-report cases on the desk this season.

options.label: Fine $1.5M + round 1 pick + coach off the sideline 2 games
options.blurb: Fined $1.5M, coach off the sideline 2 games, loses a round 1 pick

cases.title: Late hit on a ball carrier
cases.where: Fiota Bay T-Rexes at North Hatesei Bees, week 11
cases.text:
Nadia Ultreimyr (DL, Bees) was flagged for unnecessary roughness with 4:08 left in the first quarter on a hit the officials ruled came well after the play was over. Santiago Herrnueva (WR, T-Rexes) left for a few plays and returned. Film review showed the contact was close to the whistle. It happened in front of a national television audience.

Nadia Ultreimyr's agent, Beatrix Lund, says the player will cooperate with the review.

cases.title: Confrontation with a fan
cases.where: Wolford Dragons at Ediville Brass Tigers, week 11
cases.text:
Ruolan Xuegang (OL, Dragons) was filmed shoving a phone away from a fan outside the visitors' locker room. Video of the exchange circulated on social media.

Stadium security filed a report with the league.
